task.question: What monosaccharide was detected in the interstellar molecular cloud in July 2026?
task.evidence: 13 July – Astronomers report the detection of erythrulose, a four-carbon monosaccharide, in the interstellar molecular cloud G+0.693−0.027 near the Galactic Center. The discovery is described as the first detection of a "true sugar" in the interstellar medium, distinguishing it from previously identified sugar-related molecules such as glycolaldehyde.

[Erythrulose] D-Erythrulose (also known as erythrulose) is the organic compound with the formula HOCH2C(O)CH(OH)CH2OH (alternative notation as C4H8O4). As a ketone-containing monosaccharide, it is classified as a ketose and tetrose. Erythrulose is a colorless, sweet-tasting, water-soluble solid. Among the sugars, it is relatively obscure, being described as a "novelty tetrose". In 2026, broadband spectral surveys using large Earth-based telescopes detected erythrulose on dust grains in molecular clouds near the center of the Milky Way. | other articles: 2026 in science, List of interstellar and circumstellar molecules
